_comment: The evaluation set, rewritten for the 112-article corpus.
WHY IT WAS REWRITTEN. At 20 articles the previous set could not fail:
every answerable question had exactly one plausible home, so 100% recall
measured topic SEPARATION, not retrieval. The lead's criticism was
precise -- 'at 20 the search finds the right one no matter how bad it is,
so the score tells you nothing.'
At 112 articles the corpus has real clusters: 7 articles mention SQLite,
3 cover Django, 35 discuss agents, 25 discuss benchmarks/evaluation.
That makes three question types possible that simply could not exist
before, and this set is weighted toward them:
disambiguation  several articles cover the topic; ONE holds the answer.
Retrieving 'a SQLite article' is no longer success.
specificity     the topic is densely covered; the fact appears once.
near-miss       (in `unanswerable`) a plausible question on a densely
covered topic where the fact is ABSENT. These score in
the 0.4-0.6 band, clear the floor, and force the prompt
layer to work. At 20 articles only one question did
this; the whole false-answer rate depends on them.
Ground truth was established by reading the articles. One question in the
previous set was wrong because I assumed an article's content from its
title -- the SQLite post DOES discuss Postgres, and the system was right
while the question was wrong. Every fact below was checked against text.
